title: Structured observability audit and redaction policies for traces & logs
creator: Aisha Rao
description:
Scope:
Implement a consistent data-governance layer across tracing hooks, metrics/log pipelines, and latency/error dashboards to ensure sensitive data is redacted, retention policies are enforced, and access is auditable. This ticket covers pipeline components, runtime tracing instrumentation, access logging for observability consoles, and the initial Console UI indicators for redaction/retention status.

Goals:
- Introduce span-level PII classification and redaction at the ingestion pipeline for traces and logs.
- Add retention lifecycle automation (hot -> warm -> cold -> purge) for telemetry with per-customer overrides.
- Enforce RBAC controls and generate immutable access/audit events when observability data is accessed or exported.
- Provide console-facing metadata (redaction applied, retention window, last access) in dashboards and trace viewers.

Out of scope:
- Full multi-tenant encryption at rest (handled by KMS integration ticket ENG-8050).
- Long-term legal hold workflows (tracked in PM-412).

Non-functional requirements:
- Redaction must add < 2ms overhead per span at ingestion for 95th percentile.
- Retention enforcement job must scale to 100M events/day across clusters.
- Access audit events must be retained for 365 days in compliance storage.
tasks: Add redaction processor to trace ingestion pipeline (platform/telemetry service)
Extend log pipeline (vector/otel collector) with classification rules and masking transforms
Implement per-tenant retention metadata store and enforcement worker
Add Access-Audit event emitter on Console data fetch endpoints
Console UI: show redaction badge + retention countdown on trace/log view
E2E tests: synthetic traces with PII and verification of redaction and access logs
Performance tests: benchmark ingestion latency with redaction enabled
acceptance_criteria: Span and log PII are redacted before being written to long-term storage (verified via e2e test)
Retention lifecycle moves data between tiers and purges according to tenant policy (test dataset validated)
Access to traces/logs generates an audit event with user, resource, action, and sampled context
Console shows redaction status and retention window on trace and log detail pages
Benchmarks demonstrate <2ms median overhead and <10ms 95th percentile overhead for redaction in ingestion path
comments: 2025-11-10 Aisha Rao: Created ticket. Initial scope set after PM sync. Blocking: need final security classification taxonomy from Rahul.

2025-11-12 Diego Martinez: Spike completed for span-level redaction approach. Chose regex+tokenizer pipeline with allowlist for structured fields to avoid overmasking. Draft PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/1294
2025-11-14 Claire Thompson (PM): Confirmed tenant-specific retention windows required. PM-412 will provide UI flows for admins to set overrides.

2025-11-16 Rahul Singh (Security): Reviewed redaction approach. Concern: deterministic hashing of user identifiers may still be reversible if salted poorly. Recommendation: use per-tenant salt stored in KMS and rotate annually. Security review required before release.

2025-11-18 Diego Martinez: Implemented access-audit emitter. Currently logs to kafka topic telemetry-audit.v1. Need schema approved by infra (ENG-8050). Sample event: {user, team, resource_id, resource_type, action, timestamp, trace_id}
2025-11-20 QA: Found race in retention worker when tenant override changes mid-run. Mitigation: add versioned retention policy and idempotent deletion operations.

2025-11-22 Diego Martinez: Performance benchmarks attached to PR. Median overhead 0.9ms, 95th 3.8ms on worst-case payloads; still need optimization for larger spans. Filed follow-up ENG-8187 for kernel-level batching improvements.

2025-11-25 Claire Thompson (PM): Approving rollout to staging after security checklist items (KMS salt, schema registry) are resolved. Plan: staged rollout to 10 pilot tenants for two weeks then enable globally.
open_questions: Should we support on-the-fly allowlist edits for structured fields or require config deploys?
What’s the SLA for the retention worker handling tenant overrides during in-flight deletions?
Exact schema for access-audit events and retention policy versioning (need infra sign-off)
